title: Electron configurations
objectives: Describe the shapes of s and p orbitals and the capacity of each sub-level.
Apply the Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle and Hund's rule.
Write full and condensed configurations for atoms and ions up to Z = 36.
Explain the configurations of chromium and copper.

explanation.heading: Shells, sub-levels and orbitals
body: Each shell n contains sub-levels: s, p, d and f. Each sub-level is made of orbitals: regions where there is a high probability of finding an electron.

• s: 1 orbital, spherical, holds 2 electrons.
  • p: 3 orbitals (pₓ, p_y, p_z), dumbbell-shaped, hold 6 electrons.
  • d: 5 orbitals, hold 10 electrons.
  • f: 7 orbitals, hold 14 electrons.
The Pauli exclusion principle: an orbital holds at most two electrons, and they must have opposite spins.

explanation.heading: Filling order
body: Electrons fill the lowest-energy sub-level available first (the Aufbau principle). The order is 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p …. Importantly, 4s fills before 3d, which is why potassium and calcium come before the transition metals.
Hund's rule: in a set of orbitals of equal energy, electrons occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins before any pair up. So nitrogen's 2p³ has three unpaired electrons, one in each p orbital.

explanation.heading: Ions and exceptions
body: Once 3d is occupied, it drops below 4s in energy. So when a transition metal forms an ion, it loses its 4s electrons first: Fe is [Ar]3d⁶4s², but Fe²⁺ is [Ar]3d⁶.

Two elements in the first transition series break the simple filling order: Cr is [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ and Cu is [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹. A half-filled or completely filled d sub-level is especially stable, and the 4s and 3d energies are close enough that moving one electron is worth it.

demo.intro: Explore the orbital shapes, fill the periodic table in Aufbau order, then compare iron with the chromium and copper exceptions.
notice: The s, p and d blocks of the periodic table line up with the sub-level being filled.
The diagonal fill order puts 4s before 3d.
Cr and Cu each move one electron from 4s into 3d.

steps.do: The three 2p electrons go into separate p orbitals with parallel spins

takeaways: s, p, d, f hold 2, 6, 10, 14 electrons; each orbital holds 2 with opposite spins.
Fill 4s before 3d, but remove 4s first when forming ions.
